title: Unified onboarding schema and pin-validation playbook for newly ingested models
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Purpose: create a single, auditable onboarding schema and an operational playbook that 1) produces a reproducible model fingerprint, 2) emits a stable pin/hash for runtime pinning, 3) bundles a performance profile artifact (latency/throughput/memory baselines + recommended runtime knobs), and 4) documents exact gating steps and docs changes required before a model variant lands in the public catalog. This ticket standardizes metadata fields, validation rules, and the docs/PR workflow so new models (including quantized variants) can be onboarded with minimal manual review while preserving production safety and performance guarantees.
acceptance_criteria: A canonical onboarding schema JSON/YAML example is published and stored in the catalog repo
A deterministic fingerprinting script (weights+tokenizer+config -> SHA256) is added to the ingest pipeline and produces stable hashes during CI runs
Pin validation job exists: given a candidate pin it verifies model load, tokenization consistency, and end-to-end smoke prompts (pass/fail)

Performance profile artifact format defined (fields: seq_lengths, median_latency_ms@N, p95_latency_ms@N, tokens_per_second, peak_gpu_mem_mb, recommended_batch_size, kv_cache_policy, quantization_note)
Automated perf runner publishes artifacts to catalog-artifacts and writes a reference entry in model_manifest with a stable profile URL
Docs: onboarding checklist, PR template, and 'pinning best practices' doc added to docs/model-catalog and referenced from Console onboarding flow
Gate: new model variant cannot be published without at least 2 independent perf runs and a PM or SRE sign-off recorded in the ticket

decision_log: Fingerprinting: use SHA256 of a canonical tarball containing {model_weights, tokenizer_config, generation_config} to maximize determinism. Decision made 2026-02-12 after spike.
Pin semantics: pins are 'manifest-pins' (weight+tokenizer+config) and not the upstream model tag. Rationale: reproducibility and protection from upstream force-pushes. Decided 2026-02-14.
Performance runs: require at least two independent CI runs using different runners to catch transient variance. Use median across runs. Decided 2026-02-16.
Release policy: auto-publish to internal catalog after CI+SRE smoke pass. Public publish requires PM sign-off and docs entry. Decided 2026-02-19.
Docs UX: include a small 'Console-ready summary' JSON that Console can render on the model card (max 3 key metrics). Decided 2026-02-25.
Quantized models: require quantization-note and hardware-compatibility matrix; do not auto-pin quantized artifacts without an explicit 'quantization_certified' flag. Decided 2026-02-26.
License checks: add an automated license scanner to CI. If license is unknown or incompatible, block publish. Decided 2026-02-22.
Rollout: staged publish with canary tag for 48 hours on non-critical tenants before full catalog exposure. Decided 2026-02-27.
Fallback policy: if pinned model fails in production, Router will fallback to nearest compatible variant and an alert will create an incident ticket. Decided 2026-02-28.

qa_checks: Tokenization consistency: run canonical tokenization test vectors and compare token IDs
Deterministic generation: given a fixed seed, verify top_k/top_p deterministic output for a short prompt across two runners
Latency regressions: compare median latency at seq=128 against baseline; block if >20% regression or p95 > baseline*1.3
Memory sanity: confirm peak GPU memory < configured safety margin for target hardware (A100 80GB by default)
License scanner: must return 'compatible' or 'permitted with conditions' for publish
